text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'dedicated-eu-2' queue depth > 1200, tail latency p99 4.2s, 5xx spike from 0.3% -> 6.1% in last 3m. Auto-scale events throttled. Paging on-call.

alex (oncall): got the page, I'm on it. seeing the same in grafana. A bunch of requests are queued and some are hitting model fallbacks.

alex (oncall): quick assessment — traffic spike appears to be concentrated from a few orgs (org-324, org-198). Likely a customer batch job. Dedicated pool CPU/GPU utilization is at 98%. Autoscaler isn't adding new nodes fast enough; burst capacity is disabled for this pool.

priya: +1. can we enable burst capacity temporarily and switch to an aggressive autoscale policy? that should buy us headroom while we coordinate with the customer.

alex (oncall): I'm going to do a controlled toggle. will first add a temporary rate limit for non-enterprise orgs to reduce noise, then flip burst on for dedicated-eu-2.

liz (support): heads up — support already has a ticket open from org-324 complaining about timeouts. i'll message them that we're doing mitigations; please include ETA.

alex (oncall): taking action now. commands i will run:

```bash
# apply soft rate limit for non-enterprise traffic (global)
rbctl rate-limits set --scope non-enterprise --qps 50 --reason "temporary surge mitigation"

# toggle burst capacity on the dedicated pool and set autoscale policy
rbctl dedicated pools update --id dedicated-eu-2 --burst-enabled true --burst-multiplier 3 --autoscale-policy aggressive

# disable high-cost streaming endpoint for non-enterprise orgs (short window)
rbctl routes update --route /v1/generate/stream --override-rate-limit non-enterprise=0 --reason "mitigation"
```

deploy-bot: rbctl: executing update on pool dedicated-eu-2. request queued.

alex (oncall): rbctl returned OK. burst enabled, multiplier 3, autoscale policy aggressive. monitoring for new nodes to attach.

sre-ops: seeing new instances provisioning. GPU attach lag ~25s, queue depth decreasing from 1200 -> 420 in last 60s. p95 dropped from 1.8s -> 750ms.

priya: great. keep the temporary rate limit in place until we confirm normal queue behaviour for 10m. also can we open a short-lived quota override for org-324 since they're paying enterprise? that will keep their customer UX good while we stabilize others.

alex (oncall): granting quota override for org-324. command:

```bash
rbctl orgs quota update --org org-324 --burst-qps 200 --reason "enterprise override during surge"
```

deploy-bot: quota updated for org-324.

liz (support): notified org-324: "We observed a traffic surge affecting latency; we've enabled temporary capacity and given you an override. We'll follow up once stabilized." They replied: "thanks, pushing a smaller job now."

darren: moving to 2nd-line handoff. alex — if you need me to take over the remediation window, say so. I'm available.

alex (oncall): handing off at +20. I'm going offline for the next scheduled meeting but will check back at +10. notes: burst=on, autoscale=aggressive, global non-enterprise qps=50, org-324 override=200, streaming disabled for non-enterprise.

sre-ops: additional mitigation suggestion: enable short-term traffic shaping on the inference-router to favor lower-cost models for public customers (map heavy requests to quantized variants) — can be done via routing policy change:

```yaml
# routing policy snippet
- match: org not in enterprise
  route: model-family/quantized-variants
  weight: 0.8
  fallback: original
```

alex (oncall): don't change routing without QA, but we can enable a temporary policy with fallback and low weight. will validate with small percentage rollout (canary 5%).

alex (oncall): status update after 5m: queue depth 120 -> 80, p99 now 1.1s, 5xx down to 1.2%. Burst capacity has added 4 nodes. autoscaler reports headroom for next 10m.

priya: recommend keeping burst enabled for 30m and then re-evaluate. if things remain stable, we can reduce burst multiplier to 1.5 before fully disabling.

liz (support): customers impacted list compiled: org-324 (enterprise, override), org-198 (dev, received 504s), org-776 (dev, degraded). I've sent templated messages to org-198 and org-776 explaining rate limits and ETA.

darren: logging handoff: i'm now primary for the incident window. alex — thanks, leave any runbook notes. i'll watch the dashboard and coordinate with infra for any node failures.

alex (oncall): runbook note added to incident document: "enable burst, set autoscale->aggressive, apply non-enterprise QPS=50, org-324 override, disable streaming for non-enterprise, monitor queues and p99. revert after stable 30m window."

sre-ops: monitoring looks good. recommending we keep mitigations for 25 more minutes then perform a staged rollback: first remove non-enterprise rate limit, then reduce burst multiplier, then set autoscale back to standard.

darren: agreed. i'll coordinate rollback at T+30 unless anyone objects.

liz (support): will update support ticket statuses and post a short note to status.redwood.ai stating: "We experienced a transient surge affecting Dedicated EU pool; mitigations applied. Customers with ongoing issues should contact support."

alex (oncall): final note — please capture cost impact (burst nodes + override) and record in incident for chargeback. tagging product/ops for follow-up to discuss autoscale threshold tuning to avoid repeated manual toggles. :chart_with_upwards_trend: 

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: mitigations applied at 2620001239, monitoring healthy. last update 2620001299.
